page: Amazon Web Services r7i.24xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by the Nitro hypervisor and custom Intel Xeon 8488C processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system operates at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz and includes a 105 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. The instance does not include local NVMe storage or dedicated GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage and offering a baseline network bandwidth of 38 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance, with the Passmark CPU score and CPU encryption tests reaching the top 10% tier. The DDR5 memory subsystem delivers strong read and write bandwidth, registering 228.17 GB/sec for large block uncached reads and 95.44 GB/sec for large block uncached writes. The processor's advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512, contribute to strong performance in specialized tasks. For instance, Geekbench image processing ranks in the top 10% tier, while LLM inference for prompt processing on medium and large models falls within the top 25% tier.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8:1 and the absence of bundled local storage or GPUs, this instance is structured for memory-intensive workloads that require substantial RAM capacity without the overhead of local disk management. The qualitative cost profile reflects a premium hardware class optimized for high resource density. It is highly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, such as Redis, where it achieves 98.08 million operations per second in SET benchmarks. Other appropriate workloads include enterprise database management, high-throughput web serving, software compilation, and memory-bound data processing pipelines.
